PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE A SUPPLEMENTAL
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF HIS RULE 26(d)(1) MOTION, ECF NO. 15,
ADDRESSING NCMEC’S SEPTEMBER 18, 2026 FILING

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) for leave to file the
supplemental memorandum attached as Exhibit A. Exhibit A supports Plaintiffs pending motion
under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1). ECF No. 15. In support, Plaintiff states as follows.

1. ECF No. 15 requests leave to serve three interrogatories on Defendant National
Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”) before the Rule 26(f) conference. The three
interrogatories appear at ECF No. 15-1. Each permits three answers: “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable to
determine after reasonable inquiry.” The interrogatories seek no explanation and no report content.

2. On September 18, 2026, Defendants Katie Hall and NCMEC filed their opposition
to Plaintiff’s motion for leave to file a Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint. ECF No.

74. ECF No. 74 describes the statements at issue as concerning CyberTipline reports received “for

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 78 Filed 09/18/26 Page 2 of 7 PagelD# 778

any of the three identifiers in Plaintiff’s subpoena to NCMEC.” ECF No. 74 at 5. ECF No. 74 states
that Plaintiff “cannot plausibly assert falsity, because he does not have access to those reports,” and
that “[nJo allegations Plaintiff can make can change that fact.” Id.

3. Those statements renew the factual premise the three interrogatories test. Exhibit A
places ECF No. 74’s formulations beside the pending interrogatories. Exhibit A explains why the
three answers bear on the relief NCMEC now seeks.

4. The discovery request is unchanged. Exhibit A proposes no new interrogatory.
Exhibit A changes no exclusion, no permitted answer, and no responding party. The supplement
changes the decisional record, not the request.

5. This motion does not withdraw or modify the objections or the relief requested in
ECF Nos. 66-68.

6. Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) provides that no further briefs may be filed without leave
of Court. Plaintiff seeks that leave. A Memorandum in Support accompanies this motion.

7. Conferral. This motion seeks briefing permission under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1),
relief that only the Court can grant. The discovery matters at issue are the three interrogatories in
ECF No. 15-1. Those matters were the subject of the conference certified with ECF No. 15, and
that certification stands. On September 18, 2026, Plaintiff sent counsel for Defendants Katie Hall
and NCMEC this motion package, requested a telephone conference concerning the relief
requested, and proposed September 21, 2026 for the call. Counsel responded that he was not
available on the proposed date and stated: “My clients do not consent.” The motion is opposed.

8. Relief requested. Plaintiff requests an order (a) granting leave to file the
supplemental memorandum attached as Exhibit A; (b) deeming Exhibit A filed for consideration

with ECF No. 15; (c) providing for any responsive submission the Court authorizes; and (d)

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 78 Filed 09/18/26 Page 3 of 7 PagelD# 779

determining this motion before disposition of ECF No. 15. Adjudication of ECF No. 15 remains for

the Court’s ruling on that motion. A proposed order accompanies this motion.

Date: September 18, 2026 Respectfully submitted,

Marvelle J. Ballentine

GENERATIVE-ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE DISCLOSURE AND

CITATION CERTIFICATION PURSUANT TO ECF NOS. 63 AND 65

Pursuant to the Orders entered September 9, 2026 (ECF No. 63) and September 10, 2026
(ECF No. 65), Plaintiff states as follows.

1. Identification of use. Plaintiff used generative artificial intelligence in the
preparation of the Motion, Exhibit A (the Proposed Supplemental Memorandum), the Proposed
Order, and the Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument submitted with this filing. The assistance
consisted of research, drafting, and revision of text; retrieval of docket entries and filed documents
from the public RECAP archive; and verification of record citations against the docket. Plaintiff
reviewed, edited, and adopted each document as his own submission. The Proposed Order is
covered by this certification and carries no separate certification on its face. Exhibit A carries its
own disclosure and certification so that the document stands compliant if deemed filed. The
Memorandum in Support is separately filed and carries its own disclosure and certification.

2. Citation review. Plaintiff certifies that he has reviewed each citation to legal
authority and each citation to the record in the documents identified in paragraph 1 for accuracy.
Plaintiff performed that review using automated citation-verification tools to verify cited
authorities against published sources and by comparing each record citation to the document as
docketed.

3. Method. ECF Nos. 63 and 65 do not specify the form or placement of this
disclosure. Plaintiff places the disclosure and certification in each motion filing and separately
docketed memorandum, with the motion’s certification expressly covering the AlJ-assisted
attachments identified in paragraph 1. Plaintiff supplies this disclosure and certification while

maintaining the authority-and-scope objection stated in Part IX of the Memorandum in Support of

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 78 Filed 09/18/26 Page 7 of 7 PagelD# 783

his Rule 72(a) Objections. ECF No. 68. Plaintiff requests approval of this method, or specification
of a different method, for any requirement that remains in effect.
